# Rule reference

<!-- Generated by `repoproof rules --format markdown`; edit the rule texts in src/repoproof/models.py. -->

Every finding carries a rule ID. The severity shown is the default; a few rules lower it when the evidence is weaker (see the rule text).

| ID | Name | Default severity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [RP001](#rp001) | `docs-not-found` | warning |
| [RP101](#rp101) | `command-failed` | error |
| [RP102](#rp102) | `command-timeout` | error |
| [RP103](#rp103) | `command-not-found` | error |
| [RP104](#rp104) | `environment-setup-failed` | error |
| [RP105](#rp105) | `isolation-unavailable` | error |
| [RP201](#rp201) | `broken-link` | error |
| [RP202](#rp202) | `broken-anchor` | warning |
| [RP301](#rp301) | `env-undocumented` | warning |
| [RP302](#rp302) | `env-missing-from-example` | warning |

| [RP304](#rp304) | `env-not-in-deployment` | note |

## RP001

**`docs-not-found`** · default severity: warning

A documentation file to verify could not be found.

RepoProof looks for README.md by default. Name the files to verify under `[repoproof] docs` in repoproof.toml.

## RP101

**`command-failed`** · default severity: error

A documented command exited with a non-zero status.

A new developer following the documentation would be stuck at this step. Fix the command, the instructions around it, or the repository itself.

## RP102

**`command-timeout`** · default severity: error

A documented command did not finish in time.

Raise `[sandbox] timeout` (or a per-phase value in `[sandbox.timeouts]`) if the step is legitimately slow. Otherwise the command probably waits for input or never exits (servers and file watchers do not belong in a verified journey).

## RP103

**`command-not-found`** · default severity: error

A documented command is not available in a clean environment.

The executable is not installed and no earlier documented step installs it. Document the prerequisite or add the missing install step.

## RP104

**`environment-setup-failed`** · default severity: error

RepoProof could not prepare the clean environment.

Usually the Python `venv` module is unavailable (Debian/Ubuntu: install `python3-venv`) or the temporary directory is not writable.

## RP105

**`isolation-unavailable`** · default severity: error

Strict isolation was requested but cannot be enforced on this host.

Network restrictions need Linux with unprivileged user namespaces. Run on such a host, inside a disposable container or VM, or drop `strict`.

## RP201

**`broken-link`** · default severity: error

A relative link points to a file or directory that does not exist.

Paths are checked case-sensitively, like GitHub does, so a link that works on a case-insensitive laptop can still be broken for everyone else.

## RP202

**`broken-anchor`** · default severity: warning

A link points to a heading or anchor that does not exist.

Anchors are derived from headings using GitHub's slug rules. Renaming a heading silently breaks every link to it.

## RP301

**`env-undocumented`** · default severity: warning

An environment variable is read by the code but documented nowhere.

Add it to the README or to .env.example. The finding is a warning when the code shows no default for the variable and a note otherwise.

## RP302

**`env-missing-from-example`** · default severity: warning

A required variable is documented but missing from .env.example.

People copy .env.example to get started. Variables that are missing from it fail at runtime after an otherwise successful setup.

## RP303

**`env-stale-example`** · default severity: note

A variable listed in .env.example is never read by the code or deployment config.

Remove it, or ignore it with `[env] ignore` if a library reads it indirectly.

## RP304

**`env-not-in-deployment`** · default severity: note

A required variable is not set in the deployment configuration.

Checked against docker-compose files, Dockerfiles and Kubernetes manifests that declare environment variables.
